trip.name: Japan Family Trip 2026
trip.subtitle: Javier, Rikke, Saga and Leo
trip.dna: Rikke's first time in Japan. Equal mix of culture, nature, food and fun. No amusement parks. Tattoo-friendly onsen strategy throughout.

days.title: Before We Go
days.subtitle: Counting down

items: Everyone writes their sealed predictions before the airport
Pack: light layers, walking shoes, compact umbrella, day backpacks
Set both iPhones to Most Compatible so photos are JPEG not HEIC
Buy the Japan eSIM (Ubigi, Airalo or Mobal) and activate on landing
Each kid researches one place and writes a card for the site

days.title: Departure Day
days.subtitle: The long way east
days.transit: CPH to Haneda, departing 12:45. Overnight in the air, landing 07:55 tomorrow.

items: Final packing and bag weigh-in
Passports, passport copies, eSIM ready to activate on landing
Airport. Seal everyone's predictions before boarding
First post to the site from the departure lounge
Board. Sleep as much as the seats allow

days.title: Arrival, Senso-ji and the First Konbini
days.subtitle: Landing 07:55. Jet lag day, keep it gentle.
days.transit: Land at Haneda 07:55. Keikyu Line to Shinagawa (~20 min, ¥300), then on to Shinjuku.

items: Land at Haneda. Suica cards at the airport or straight into Apple Wallet
Drop bags. Check-in unlikely before 15:00, so coin lockers or luggage storage
First konbini run: onigiri, egg sandwiches, melon pan, canned coffee. This is a ritual, not a compromise
Senso-ji, Asakusa. Rikke's first temple, through the Kaminarimon gate and down Nakamise-dori
Street snacks: ningyo-yaki, age-manju, melon pan
Slow walk along the Sumida River toward the Skytree, visible the whole way
Early izakaya dinner. Yakitori, edamame, gyoza
Back by 20:00. Jet lag will crush everyone

days.title: Tsukiji, Gardens and the Skytree
days.subtitle: Markets in the morning, the whole city at night

items: Tsukiji Outer Market food crawl. Tamagoyaki on a stick, tuna cheek skewers, fresh uni, strawberry daifuku. Budget ¥3,000 to ¥5,000 each for grazing
Hama-rikyu Gardens, ten minutes away. Edo-era garden with a teahouse on the pond. Matcha and wagashi
Shibuya Crossing at dusk, the scramble from above
Shibuya Sky observation deck if the timing works
Tokyo Skytree. Tembo Deck and Tembo Galleria, timed for sunset around 17:30
Dinner at Solamachi in the mall below: ramen, tonkatsu, curry

bookings.title: Tokyo Skytree
bookings.note: Tembo Deck + Galleria combo. Time for sunset ~17:30.

days.title: Shrines, Harajuku and teamLab
days.subtitle: Culture, pop culture, then the lights

items: Meiji Jingu. Massive torii, forest-wrapped approach, maybe a wedding procession. Walk on through Yoyogi Park
Takeshita Street, Harajuku. Saga's territory: crepes, fashion, pop culture shops
Harajuku Gyoza Lou, or walk Omotesando for something more elevated
Akihabara. Leo's paradise: arcades, gachapon, manga shops, retro games. Budget ¥2,000 to ¥3,000 for tokens and capsules
teamLab. Budget two to three hours and don't rush Rikke through it
Pack for Kyoto

bookings.title: teamLab Tokyo
bookings.note: Timed entry. Dark venue, so the Pocket 3 is the better camera.

days.title: Shinkansen South, Then a Thousand Torii
days.subtitle: Tokyo to Kyoto, and straight into the vermilion
days.transit: Tokaido Shinkansen, 2h 15m. Fuji on the right-hand side, seats D and E, on a clear day.

items: Check out. Ekiben from the Gransta food halls under Tokyo Station. This is a travel ritual, take your time choosing
Board. Watch for Fuji
Arrive Kyoto around 12:30, drop bags in Gion
Fushimi Inari Taisha in the golden afternoon light. The first 20 to 30 minutes give the iconic shots, and the upper trails thin out dramatically
Inari sushi from a stall in the Fushimi backstreets
Gion evening walk down Hanami-koji. Maiko heading to engagements around 17:30 to 18:00
Dinner in Pontocho Alley. Riverside terraces run until 30 September

days.title: Gold, Zen and Bamboo
days.subtitle: Northwest Kyoto and Arashiyama

items: Kinkaku-ji at the 09:00 opening to beat the crowds. Thirty or forty minutes is plenty
Ryoan-ji, the most famous zen rock garden in the world. You can never see all fifteen stones at once. Let Leo try
Arashiyama Bamboo Grove, before noon while it is still walkable
% Arabica by the river, then soba or udon nearby
Monkey Park Iwatayama. Twenty-minute hike up to wild macaques and a panorama of Kyoto
Or the Hozugawa river boat, 16 km down the gorge (¥4,100 adult, ¥2,700 child, about 2 hours)
Casual dinner in Arashiyama, or back in Gion

days.title: Nishiki Market and teamLab Kyoto
days.subtitle: Kyoto's kitchen, then the lights again

items: Nishiki Market, Kyoto's kitchen. A covered arcade of a hundred-plus stalls: dashimaki tamago, yuba, tsukemono, matcha sweets, tako tamago. Budget ¥3,000 to ¥5,000 each
Optional family cooking class. Hana Cooking, WAK Japan or via Cookly. Around ¥7,000 to ¥10,000 each including the meal you cook
teamLab Kyoto
Gion food crawl in small plates: kushikatsu, lighter chicken-based Kyoto ramen, then wagashi and matcha at a teahouse

days.title: Nara: Deer, and the Great Buddha
days.subtitle: A day trip out of Kyoto

items: Nara Park. Twelve hundred deer roaming free, and they bow for shika senbei crackers. Leo will not want to leave
Todai-ji. The Great Buddha Hall is one of the largest wooden buildings in the world and the bronze Buddha inside is 15 metres tall
The pillar at the back of the hall with a hole the size of the Buddha's nostril. Children squeeze through it for good luck
Kakinoha-zushi, sushi wrapped in persimmon leaves. The Nara speciality
Or warabimochi and kudzu sweets around Sanjo-dori
Kasuga Taisha. Three thousand stone and bronze lanterns along the approach through the forest
Isuien Garden if there is time, small and beautifully composed
Back to Kyoto in the late afternoon
Last Kyoto dinner. Kaiseki is the splurge, ¥8,000 to ¥15,000 each
Pack for Osaka

days.transit: Kyoto to Nara on the Kintetsu limited express, about 35 minutes.

days.title: Osaka in Two Words: Eat Everything
days.subtitle: Shinsekai, the castle, and then Dotonbori
days.transit: Kyoto to Osaka on the JR Special Rapid, 30 minutes.

items: Shinsekai. Retro neon with Tsutenkaku Tower over the narrow streets
Kushikatsu at Daruma or Yaekatsu. One rule: never double-dip the communal sauce
Osaka Castle. The grounds and the top-floor view are the point
Kuromon Market, Osaka's kitchen. Giant grilled scallops, crab legs, uni, mochi
Dotonbori. The Glico running man, canal reflections, neon overload
Takoyaki at Wanaka or Kukuru, watching them turned in the moulds
Okonomiyaki at Mizuno or Fukutaro, gyoza at Chao Chao, and Cremia soft serve
Walk the canal after dark. Rikke will remember this night

days.title: teamLab Osaka and Ura-Namba
days.subtitle: Vintage streets by day, botanical lights by night

items: Amerikamura. Osaka's street culture district: vintage clothing, record shops, street art. Saga territory
Okonomiyaki you cook yourself on the teppan at your table. Kiji at the Umeda Sky Building is legendary
Umeda Sky Building floating garden observatory while you are there
Spa World in Shinsekai. Check the current tattoo policy first, it has moved toward tattoo-friendly access on certain days
Or the Museum of Housing and Living, a full-scale Edo-era Osaka street indoors
teamLab Botanical Garden, Nagai Park. Always better after dark
Ura-Namba back alleys afterwards: tiny standing bars and yakitori. Lively rather than rowdy, kids welcome
Or Hozenji Yokocho, the stone-paved alley with the moss-covered statue

bookings.title: teamLab Osaka
bookings.note: Botanical Garden, Nagai Park. Outdoors and after dark.

days.title: Peace Memorial Park
days.subtitle: The reason for the stop. Don't rush it.
days.transit: Osaka to Hiroshima, Sanyo Shinkansen, 1h 30m. Arrive around 11:00.

items: The A-Bomb Dome, preserved exactly as the blast left it
Peace Memorial Museum. Deeply moving, and the personal artifacts section is devastating. Saga at 13 is the right age to absorb this
Children's Peace Monument. For Leo, the Sadako paper cranes story is the way in
The Cenotaph and the Flame of Peace, which frames the Dome through its arch
Budget two to three hours minimum
Decompress. Walk or cycle along the river. The contrast between the park's weight and the city's vitality is the thing to notice
Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki, layered rather than mixed, with yakisoba built in
Okonomimura, a whole building of teppan counters, or Nagata-ya for the famous version

days.title: The Floating Torii
days.subtitle: Deer, oysters, and the island after the day-trippers leave
days.transit: JR to Miyajimaguchi (~30 min) then the JR ferry (10 min). Pay with the IC card.

items: Ship the large luggage ahead to Kanazawa by Takkyubin, around ¥2,000 a bag. Travel with day bags only
The ferry approach, with the floating torii of Itsukushima in view. Check the tide tables: low tide lets you walk to the gate, high tide makes it float
Itsukushima Shrine, vermilion and built out over the water. One of Japan's Three Views
The five-storey pagoda and Senjokaku Hall, a vast tatami-floored wooden hall that is often completely empty
Daishoin Temple. Hundreds of small statues in knitted caps, spinning prayer wheels, and caves lined with pilgrimage icons. The tactile stuff makes this a hit with kids
Grilled oysters from the street stalls, ¥200 to ¥500 each
Momiji manju, and the fried age-momiji version: crisp outside, molten inside
Mt Misen. Ropeway up (~¥1,800 return) then a 30-minute hike to the summit, with deer on the trails and views across the Seto Inland Sea
Or beach and deer time on the quieter southern paths
Check into the ryokan. Confirm the private onsen or in-room bath in advance
Kaiseki dinner with local seafood. Anago-meshi, conger eel over rice, is the island's signature
Walk the island at night. After 17:00 it empties out: the torii lit up, deer asleep in the streets, near silence

days.title: The Long Leg North
days.subtitle: Five hours of trains, then gold leaf
days.transit: Ferry, JR to Hiroshima, Sanyo Shinkansen to Shin-Osaka, then the Thunderbird to Kanazawa. Around five hours.

items: Early start. Ekiben and snacks for the journey, card games and books
Scenic run through mountains, coastline and rice paddies
The luggage arrives at SOKI separately by Takkyubin
Arrive around 15:00 to 16:00 and check in
Higashi Chaya District, the preserved geisha quarter of wooden lattice buildings and narrow lanes
Hakuza, where you can watch gold leaf being applied. Then the gold-leaf ice cream, Kanazawa's signature
Walk the Asano River in the fading light
Omi-cho Market area. Kaisendon piled with sweet shrimp, uni, crab and ikura, or a sushi counter where the chef decides. Nothing like Tokyo prices

days.title: Kenroku-en, Ninja-dera and the Swimming Pool
days.subtitle: A full Kanazawa day

items: Kenroku-en, one of the Three Great Gardens of Japan. Eleven hectares of lanterns, ponds, bridges and tea houses. Early admission at 7:00, standard at 8:00. Budget an hour and a half
Kanazawa Castle Park next door
21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art. The free zones include Leandro Erlich's Swimming Pool, where you look down through water at people walking below, then go below and look up
Kanazawa curry. Darker and richer than standard, on a steel plate with shredded cabbage. Champion Curry is the iconic spot and Leo will approve
Nagamachi Samurai District. Earthen walls, waterways, and the Nomura house with its garden viewed from inside
Ninja-dera. Trap doors, hidden stairways, escape tunnels and trick rooms. Around 45 minutes and reservation required
Nodoguro, blackthroat sea perch, Kanazawa's signature luxury fish. Grilled, simmered or as sashimi

bookings.title: Ninja-dera (Myoryu-ji)
bookings.note: Must be reserved ahead. Tour in Japanese with an English pamphlet.

days.title: Craft and Chill
days.subtitle: Slow day before the mountains

items: D.T. Suzuki Museum. The Taniguchi architecture is the real draw: reflecting pools, meditation spaces, minimalist corridors
Or the Yasue Gold Leaf Museum, where 99% of Japan's gold leaf comes from, with a hands-on pressing workshop
Omi-cho Market, round two. Morning is peak. Grilled scallops, fresh crab, tamagoyaki
Kaiten-zushi at Morimori Sushi. Conveyor belt sushi at Kanazawa fish quality is a different thing entirely
Rent bikes. Kanazawa is flat and easy
Nishi Chaya, the quieter western geisha quarter
Kutani pottery, with painting workshops at some studios
Or simply the private baths at SOKI before the mountain phase
Omakase sushi. Mid-range here is ¥5,000 to ¥8,000 each and world-class

days.title: Into the Alps
days.subtitle: Shirakawa-go on the way, then old town and Hida beef
days.transit: Kanazawa to Takayama by Nohi Bus, stopping at Shirakawa-go on the way.

items: Sanmachi Suji, three parallel streets of Edo-period merchant houses, now sake breweries and craft shops. The best-preserved old town in the Japanese Alps. Walk it slowly
Hida beef sushi, grilled wagyu on vinegared rice served on a senbei cracker, eaten standing at a street stall. A top-five food moment of the trip
Mitarashi dango, the savoury soy-glazed version rather than the sweet Tokyo kind
Sake tasting. Seven breweries in the old town, marked by the cedar balls hanging outside. Amazake for the kids
Hida beef dinner. Maruaki for affordable sets, or Center4 Hamburgers as the Leo-approved fallback
If staying out at Okuhida, the private rotenburo under the stars. One of the trip's peak moments
Shirakawa-go, a UNESCO village of gassho-zukuri farmhouses with steep thatched roofs built to shed heavy snow
The Shiroyama viewpoint over the whole valley is the photograph everyone knows
Wada House, the largest of the farmhouses, is open to walk through

food: Hida beef sushi on a senbei cracker

days.title: Morning Market and the Folk Village
days.subtitle: A full Takayama day

items: Miyagawa Morning Market along the river, open 06:00 to 12:00. Mountain pickles, produce, crafts, apple juice, hoba miso samples
Takayama Jinya, the only surviving Edo-era magistrate's office in Japan. Better than it sounds, with a good English audio guide

Hida Folk Village. An open-air museum of relocated gassho-zukuri thatched farmhouses around a mountain-backed pond, with hands-on woodworking, shibori dyeing and weaving. Budget one and a half to two hours
Takayama ramen. Thin curly noodles in a soy-based broth, simple toppings
Sake brewery deep dive. Funasaka and Harada are the standouts
Or cycle to Hida-Furukawa, a quieter Takayama with white-walled storehouses and koi-filled canals, from the film Your Name
Light early dinner. Tomorrow is a travel and hiking day
Pack for the Nakasendo

days.title: The Nakasendo: Magome to Tsumago
days.subtitle: Eight kilometres of the old road, then south to the pottery town
days.transit: Takayama to Nagoya on the JR Hida, then to Nakatsugawa and a bus to Magome. Afterwards: Nagiso to Nagoya, then Meitetsu down to Tokoname.

items: Depart Takayama early, around 07:30. Forward the large luggage on to Tokyo by Takkyubin
Train through the mountain valleys
Arrive Magome around 11:00. Bag forwarding on to Tsumago is about ¥500 a bag, so hike unburdened
Eight kilometres, two and a half to three hours at family pace with stops. Easy to moderate, well-marked forest trail
Cypress and cedar forest, the Odaki-Medaki twin waterfalls, the mountain pass, and stone-paved sections of the original road
Traditional tea houses along the way for rest and snacks
Gohei mochi, grilled rice cakes in walnut-miso sauce. The Kiso Valley speciality
Arrive Tsumago around 15:00 to 16:00. Arguably the most perfectly preserved post town in Japan: no visible power lines, no modern signage
Walk the main street once the day-trippers have gone. Wooden buildings, mountain light, near silence
On south to Tokoname for the night

food: Tea house snacks at the pass

days.title: Pottery Town, Then Back to the City
days.subtitle: Kilns and maneki-neko before the shinkansen
days.transit: Tokoname to Nagoya on the Meitetsu line, then the Tokaido Shinkansen to Tokyo, about 1h 40m.

items: The Pottery Footpath, Yakimono Sanpomichi. Kiln chimneys, walls built from stacked pots and pipes, and Tokonyan the giant maneki-neko watching the street
Tokoname is one of the Six Ancient Kilns of Japan, best known for red clay teapots. Workshops are easy to find if you want to make something
Arrive Tokyo around 14:00. Check in, luggage should be waiting via Takkyubin
Low-key wander. Yanaka old-town: the Ginza shopping street, cat statues everywhere, temple walks. Non-neon Tokyo
Yakitori Alley at Yurakucho, under the elevated tracks. Smoke, charcoal, cold beer and trains rumbling overhead

days.title: Unfinished Business
days.subtitle: Whatever you missed the first time

items: Toyosu Market. The restaurants open early for world-class sushi breakfast, so go hungry. The tuna auction deck needs a reservation
Or Ueno Park: the Tokyo National Museum, the zoo, and the chaotic Ameya-Yokocho market under the tracks
Tsukemen at Fuunji in Shinjuku. Thick rich broth, cold noodles you dip. Among Tokyo's top five ramen experiences
Odaiba and Miraikan: robots, space, interactive exhibits, and the Gundam statue outside
Or Shinjuku Gyoen with a konbini picnic
Or Nakano Broadway, a less touristy Akihabara of vintage manga and retro toys
Omoide Yokocho in Shinjuku. Tiny alleyways of yakitori stalls and ramen counters, smoky and cramped
Or a sushi omakase splurge, ¥8,000 to ¥15,000 each

days.title: Last Full Day
days.subtitle: Souvenirs, favourites, and the final dinner

items: Souvenirs. Don Quijote for the chaotic everything-store run, tax-free for tourists
Tokyu Hands and Loft for Japanese design goods and stationery
Isetan Shinjuku depachika, the gold standard for beautifully packaged sweets. This is where you buy for people back home
Tonkatsu at Maisen, tempura at Tsunahachi, or udon at Maruka
Repeat a favourite. teamLab again if Rikke wants a second round, Meiji Jingu for a last quiet temple moment, or bikes along the Sumida
Final dinner. Bookend the trip at the izakaya from night one, or robatayaki for the theatre of it, or curate a depachika picnic and eat in
Pack for departure

days.title: Homeward
days.subtitle: Early transfer to Haneda
days.transit: Haneda to CPH, departing 11:45, landing 18:15. Keikyu from Shinagawa (~20 min) or the Monorail from Hamamatsucho.

items: Early start and airport transfer
One last konbini breakfast
Fly home

days.title: After
days.subtitle: What we learned, ate, and would do again

items: Reveal everyone's sealed predictions
Each person picks their top three photos and says why
The food book: best dish per city, the ramen leaderboard, most divisive meal
Trip stats: photos taken, kilometres travelled, yen spent, konbini snacks tried
What each of us shipped on the website

packing: Comfortable walking shoes, 10,000 steps a day is the floor
Light layers: t-shirt plus a light jacket or hoodie
Rain jackets or compact umbrellas, light rain is likely
Pack for five days and use coin laundry twice
A modesty layer for temples, shoulders covered
Japan eSIM bought before departure, activated on landing

shinjuku.note: Warm and humid. The hottest part of the trip.

kyoto.note: Still warm. Two of the last four years had a genuinely wet day.

osaka.note: Three of the last four years were bone dry. 2022 had 79mm in one day.

hiroshima.note: The most reliably dry leg of the whole trip.

miyajima.note: Mild and calm. Good ferry weather every year on record.

kanazawa.note: The wettest leg. Kanazawa is famous for it. Pack the umbrellas here.

takayama.note: Noticeably cooler, especially mornings and evenings. First jacket weather.

kiso.note: Coldest mornings of the trip, around 11C, and dry all four years. Good hiking weather.

tokyo.note: Cooler than the first Tokyo block. Early autumn proper.

Nishiki Market, yudofu, obanzai, kaiseki, matcha everything

Hida beef sushi, mitarashi dango, sake
Gohei mochi, soba, mountain vegetables, iwana
